scope: the NEW packet-level features V5 adds on top of the frozen V4 52-dimensional input. The 26 flow base features and their 26 relative changes are NOT redefined here — see docs/feature_contract_v4.json, which V5 does not modify.
index_offset_note: packet features occupy indices 52..81; indices 0..51 are the frozen V4 vector in the frozen V4 order

builder.session_scope: ORDERED 5-tuple (src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, protocol); A->B and B->A are separate sessions, matching TCP's independent per-direction sequence spaces

window_semantics.origin: epoch-aligned multiples of 10 s: window_idx = floor(packet_epoch_seconds / 10) - win0
window_semantics.win0: the bin of the capture's first packet, identical to the re-basing src/pcap_ingest_v4.py:reconstruct_flows applies, so the packet-window table and the flow-window table share an index
window_semantics.rounding: floor, never round-half; no tolerance band
window_semantics.packet_ordering: packets are processed in (timestamp_abs, packet_index) order, where packet_index is the CAPTURE-ORDER ordinal. Capture timestamps are not unique, and the session-state annotations (retransmission, TCP window change) depend on observation order, so a timestamp-only sort would leave the result dependent on how rows happened to be arranged. Within one timestamp the capture order is the best available statement of what the sensor saw first. This tie-break is what makes the training-side and PCAP-side routes produce bit-identical output across a storage round-trip.
window_semantics.row_assignment: EACH PACKET is assigned to the window containing ITS OWN timestamp
window_semantics.row_assignment_difference_from_v4_flow_l: The V4 flow layer assigns a WHOLE FLOW — all of its statistics — to the window of its FIRST packet. The packet layer cannot do that: it would let packets that arrive after t+10 contribute to the state at t, which is the future-information leakage Part 19 forbids. The bin WIDTH, ORIGIN and BOUNDARY RULE are identical between the two layers; only the assignment unit differs (packet vs flow), and that difference is what makes the packet layer causal.
window_semantics.empty_windows: produce NO row, identical to the V4 flow layer. The downstream 10-second contiguity gate (np.all(diffs == 1) on window_idx) rejects any sequence spanning such a gap.
window_semantics.first_window: kept as-is; its relative-change row is forced to exactly 0.0
window_semantics.last_window: kept as-is; no packet feature ever reads forward
window_semantics.timestamp_source: the pcap per-packet capture timestamp (scapy pkt.time), i.e. the clock of the capture host at the capture point

timezone.training_csv_clock: CSE-CIC-IDS2018 CICFlowMeter CSV Timestamp is Atlantic local time (America/Halifax, UTC-4 on 2018-03-02) with the AM/PM marker dropped by the dataset authors
timezone.policy: UNCHANGED from V4. The packet layer floors UTC epoch seconds, exactly as the V4 PCAP path already does; the training path's local-clock handling is not touched. No timezone conversion is introduced anywhere by V5.
timezone.consequence: bin width and boundary rule are identical across paths, but the two clocks are not co-anchored. This matters only when aligning a PCAP window to a dataset window; it changes no feature VALUE.

safe_log1p.applied: AT window aggregation, BEFORE relative change

ratio.definition: numerator / denominator, returning EXACTLY 0.0 when denominator == 0
ratio.difference_from_v4: V4's flow rates use an epsilon-inflated denominator (x / (|y| + 1e-8)). The packet layer does not, because its denominators are exact integer packet counts: the zero case is a real, enumerable condition ('no TCP packets in this window') that should be handled explicitly and be testable, not smeared by an epsilon. This is a deliberate V5 policy choice and changes nothing about the 26 V4 features.

std.definition: sample standard deviation, ddof=1; exactly 0.0 for n <= 1

percentile.definition: numpy linear interpolation, method='linear', pinned explicitly
percentile.note: pinned so the method cannot drift with a numpy default change and silently move every p50/p90 value

entropy_from_counts.definition: Shannon entropy base 2 of value_counts(dropna=True), p + 1e-12 inside the log, 0.0 when <= 1 distinct value

nan_inf_handling.definition: the 21 packet features are replace([inf,-inf], NaN).fillna(0.0) before leaving build_packet_windows
nan_inf_handling.matches: the identical V4 policy in compute_window_features
nan_inf_handling.applied: AFTER window aggregation, BEFORE relative change

relative_change_semantics.previous_window: the immediately preceding EXISTING ROW of the packet-window table — not necessarily t-10 s, because empty windows produce no row
relative_change_semantics.reset_scope: one capture (PCAP path) / one source day (training path) — identical to V4
relative_change_semantics.log_order: computed on the ALREADY log-transformed base feature, identical to V4
relative_change_semantics.v4_semantics_unchanged: The 26 V4 relative-change features are computed by the untouched V4 code and are not re-derived, re-ordered or re-defined here.
relative_change_semantics.selection_rule: NOT every new base feature receives a relative change. 9 of 21 do. The ruling and reason for each of the 21 is in features[].relative_change_decision / relative_change_reason.

normalisation_semantics.status: NOT FITTED — a V5 scaler can only be fitted on a V5 training partition, and no V5 training partition exists (see docs/v5_packet_dataset_manifest.json). Every one of the 82 features is therefore declared 'normalised: true, scaler: pending' rather than being given a fabricated scaler.
normalisation_semantics.v4_scaler_reuse: FORBIDDEN. data/processed/multiday_benchmark_K5/input_scaler.pkl is a 52-dimensional frozen V4 artefact; it is read by V5 code only to verify its hash is unchanged, never to transform an 82-dimensional vector.
normalisation_semantics.other_transforms: none — no PCA, no whitening, no feature selection, identical to V4

content_inspection: NONE. No payload byte is read anywhere in this pipeline. Every payload feature is derived from the integer LENGTH carried in the IP/L4 headers.

features.name: ttl_mean
features.aggregation: mean over all IP packets in the window
features.formula: float(ttl.mean()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 is only reachable if every packet carried TTL 0, which a forwarded packet cannot; in practice a 0 here means the window was empty and no row was emitted
features.relative_change_reason: Denominator is a hop count that is never near zero in a non-empty window, so the ratio is numerically stable. A shift in mean hop distance between adjacent windows is exactly the 'new peer population' signal the world model should see as a transition.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: IPv4 TTL and IPv6 Hop Limit are POOLED. Both are 8-bit remaining-hop counters with identical semantics, range and decrement rule, so a pooled statistic is well defined. The choice is recorded because it is a semantic merge, not an implementation detail; IPv6 is 0.05% of packets in the available captures.

features.name: ttl_std
features.aggregation: sample standard deviation (ddof=1) over all IP packets in the window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: EXACTLY 0.0 for a constant-TTL window (all packets from one hop distance) and for a single-packet window. These two cases are not distinguishable from each other; packet_count is carried alongside so a consumer can separate them.
features.relative_change_reason: Can have a zero denominator (constant-TTL window), where the ratio saturates the +/-10 clip. That saturation is retained deliberately: constant-TTL -> varied-TTL is a genuine regime change and the clipped value is a correct 'large jump' indicator, not a numerical accident. Same behaviour the frozen V4 contract already accepts for std_pkt_len.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: ddof=1 matches the V4 std_pkt_len convention.

features.name: ttl_min
features.aggregation: min over all IP packets in the window
features.formula: float(ttl.min()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 only for an empty window (no row emitted)
features.relative_change_reason: Extreme order statistic of a bounded 8-bit field. A single distant packet moves it, so its window-to-window ratio is noise-dominated; the informative content is its LEVEL, which the base feature already carries.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Order statistic: tracks the most distant observed source. Single-packet sensitive.

features.name: ttl_max
features.aggregation: max over all IP packets in the window
features.formula: float(ttl.max()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 only for an empty window (no row emitted)
features.relative_change_reason: Extreme order statistic of a bounded 8-bit field, and in practice pinned at the initial TTL of the nearest traffic source (64/128/255), so its window-to-window ratio is almost always 0 punctuated by single-packet artefacts. Its LEVEL is the informative part.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Order statistic: tracks the nearest / locally originated traffic.

features.name: log_ttl_unique_count
features.aggregation: log1p of the number of distinct TTL values in the window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: log1p(1) = 0.693 for a constant-TTL window; a literal 0.0 means zero packets
features.relative_change_reason: Diversity/volume-like and already log-compressed, so the relative change is a stable bounded quantity. A fan-out burst appears here before it appears in the mean.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Diversity counterpart to ttl_mean. A surge in distinct TTLs indicates traffic arriving from many different hop distances in one window (scan-like fan-out, or spoofed sources).

features.name: log_tcp_window_mean
features.aggregation: mean over TCP packets in the window, then log1p
features.formula: _safe_log1p(win.mean()) where win = raw 16-bit TCP window of every TCP packet in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: no TCP packets in the window -> 0.0
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means EITHER no TCP traffic OR every advertised window was 0. Ambiguous by design, matching the V4 fillna(0.0) policy; tcp_window_zero_ratio separates the two cases.
features.relative_change_reason: Flow-control state is inherently about change: the level alone cannot distinguish a steadily small window from a window that has just collapsed.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: RAW header value: the TCP window-scale option is deliberately NOT applied, because the scale factor is only observable when the SYN handshake is inside the capture. Applying it to some connections and not others would make the feature inconsistent between windows.

features.name: log_tcp_window_std
features.aggregation: sample standard deviation (ddof=1) over TCP packets, then log1p
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 for a constant-window window, a single-TCP-packet window, and a no-TCP window alike
features.relative_change_reason: Log-compressed dispersion; the change captures the onset of heterogeneous peer behaviour.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Dispersion of advertised receive windows — wide dispersion means many peers with different buffer states inside one 10 s bin.

features.name: log_tcp_window_max
features.aggregation: max over TCP packets, then log1p
features.formula: _safe_log1p(win.max()) over the raw window field of every TCP packet in [t, t+10)
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means no TCP packets or an all-zero-window window
features.relative_change_reason: Extreme order statistic, in practice pinned at the largest advertising peer's constant value, so its relative change is ~0 with occasional single-packet spikes.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Upper extent of advertised receive capacity.

features.name: tcp_window_zero_ratio
features.aggregation: count(window == 0) / count(TCP packets), per window
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means no zero-window packets OR no TCP at all
features.relative_change_reason: Bounded proportion that is exactly 0.0 in the large majority of windows. Its relative change is then 0/0 -> epsilon-driven clip saturation, which encodes the ARRIVAL of any zero-window packet as a constant +10 regardless of magnitude. The base ratio already conveys that arrival, with magnitude, and without the saturation artefact.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Zero-window advertisements are explicit receiver flow-control stalls. Chosen over the raw tcp_window_zero_count because the count is confounded with window volume, which log_total_packets already carries.

features.name: tcp_window_change_rate
features.aggregation: count(window value differs from the same directional session's previous packet) / count(TCP packets that HAVE such a predecessor), per window
features.formula: _ratio(n_win_changed, n_win_eligible) where a packet is 'eligible' iff it is TCP and not the first packet of its directional session (ordered 5-tuple, 120 s idle reset), and 'changed' iff its raw window value differs from that predecessor's
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means every advertised window was steady, or there was no eligible TCP packet
features.relative_change_reason: Already a first-order change quantity. Its relative change is a second difference of the window-size signal: unstable, hard to interpret, and not something the 10-window LSTM context needs pre-computed.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: EXACT DEFINITION, stated because 'change rate' is otherwise ambiguous: the denominator is TCP packets WITH a predecessor, NOT all TCP packets, so the first packet of every session is excluded from both numerator and denominator. A pair that straddles a window boundary is attributed to the LATER packet's window only — never to the earlier one — which keeps the feature causal.

features.name: log_frag_packet_count
features.aggregation: log1p of the number of fragmented IP packets in the window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 for an unfragmented window — which is EVERY window in every capture available to this project (see the limitation note)
features.relative_change_reason: Structurally zero in every window of every capture available to this project. A relative change over an all-zero series is identically 0.0 and would add a dead dimension.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Fragment recognition follows RFC 791 exactly, NOT 'any nonzero flag bit': the DF bit is nonzero on 96% of real packets and means the opposite of fragmentation. first fragment = MF set AND offset == 0; middle fragment = MF set AND offset > 0; last fragment = MF clear AND offset > 0; unfragmented = MF clear AND offset == 0. IPv6 routers never fragment, so IPv6 fragmentation is read only from the Fragment extension header (M flag and offset), and an IPv6 packet without that header is unfragmented by definition.

features.name: frag_packet_ratio
features.aggregation: count(fragmented IP packets) / count(IP packets), per window
features.formula: _ratio(n_frag, n_ip) — fragmented IP packets over all IP packets in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 for an unfragmented window; identically 0.0 in all available captures
features.relative_change_reason: Structurally zero in every window of every capture available to this project, exactly as log_frag_packet_count is. A relative change over an all-zero series is identically 0.0, so including it would add a second dead dimension rather than a second signal.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Scale-free companion to log_frag_packet_count: the count detects a fragmentation flood, the ratio detects a small but wholly fragmented conversation.

features.name: ip_df_ratio
features.aggregation: count(IPv4 packets with DF set) / count(IPv4 packets), per window
features.formula: _ratio(n_df, n_ip4) — the denominator is IPv4 packets ONLY
features.missing_value_rule: no IPv4 packets in the window -> 0.0
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means no DF-marked packet, or no IPv4 packet at all
features.relative_change_reason: Bounded proportion that sits near a near-constant level (0.96 +/- 0.09 on real traffic). Its relative change is a small-amplitude, near-zero-mean quantity dominated by the traffic mix rather than by any security-relevant transition.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: IPv6 is EXCLUDED from both numerator and denominator because IPv6 has no DF bit — routers may never fragment IPv6, so 'DF' is not a property an IPv6 packet can carry, and counting IPv6 as DF=0 would fabricate a value. This is the only fragmentation-family feature with real variance in the available captures (0.96 +/- 0.09 on real traffic).

features.name: log_tcp_retrans_count
features.aggregation: log1p of the number of sequence-space re-covering TCP packets in the window
features.formula: _safe_log1p(sum(is_retransmission)); is_retransmission is True iff the packet is TCP, eff_len = payload_len + (1 if SYN) + (1 if FIN) > 0, the packet is not the first seq-bearing packet of its directional session, and seq + eff_len is at or below that session's running high-water mark under 32-bit modular comparison
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means a clean window with no re-covered sequence space, or no TCP at all
features.relative_change_reason: The one retransmission feature that earns a relative change: retransmission is bursty, and the onset of a burst (a congestion or scan event) is a transition the model should see directly. Well populated in the real captures (1.4% of seq-bearing packets, present in 24% of windows), so this is not an all-zero series.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: eff_len > 0 is the load-bearing exclusion: zero-length packets (pure ACK, window update, bare RST, keepalive) are NEVER counted, so duplicate ACKs are not mistaken for retransmissions. SYN and FIN each consume one sequence number, so SYN and FIN retransmissions ARE detected. Partial/overlapping retransmissions count only when the segment is wholly re-covered — the conservative direction. MEASURED LIMITATION: a genuinely out-of-order packet is indistinguishable from a retransmission under any high-water-mark rule, so this feature measures 'sequence-space re-coverage' = retransmission + reordering, and is named and documented as such rather than being claimed as a pure retransmission count.

features.name: tcp_retrans_ratio
features.aggregation: count(retransmissions) / count(seq-bearing TCP packets), per window
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 for a clean window or a window with no seq-bearing TCP packet
features.relative_change_reason: Bounded proportion, zero in most windows -> the same 0/0 clip-saturation problem as tcp_window_zero_ratio, and near-collinear with the count's relative change when nonzero.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: The denominator is seq-bearing packets, NOT all TCP packets: dividing by a population that cannot be retransmitted by construction would make the ratio depend on the ACK/data mix instead of on retransmission behaviour.

features.name: log_tcp_retrans_bytes
features.aggregation: log1p of the total retransmitted payload bytes in the window
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 when nothing was retransmitted AND when only zero-payload SYN/FIN were retransmitted — a real and useful distinction from log_tcp_retrans_count, which is nonzero in the second case (control-plane retransmission with no data cost)
features.relative_change_reason: Near-collinear with log_tcp_retrans_count's relative change, because both move together whenever a data retransmission burst starts. Only the count's version is kept.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Separates cheap control retransmission from expensive bulk retransmission.

features.name: payload_len_p50
features.aggregation: 50th percentile over all IP packets in the window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 is COMMON and meaningful — it means at least half the packets in the window carried no payload (ACK-dominated traffic)
features.relative_change_reason: Multiplicative shifts in typical message size are meaningful and the log-free byte scale makes the ratio directly interpretable.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Robust central tendency. Deliberately NOT a mean: V4's mean_pkt_len already carries a mean-of-flow-means of the same quantity, and a second mean would be near-collinear.

features.name: payload_len_p90
features.aggregation: 90th percentile over all IP packets in the window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means over 90% of packets were payload-free
features.relative_change_reason: Upper-tail shifts mark the start and end of bulk transfer, which is precisely a transition event.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Upper-tail shape: separates bulk transfer from control chatter independently of the median. Together with p50 this is the 'richer payload-size distribution' the problem statement asks for.

features.name: payload_len_max
features.aggregation: max over all IP packets in the window
features.formula: float(payload_len.max()) over every IP packet in [t, t+10)
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means no packet in the window carried any payload
features.relative_change_reason: Extreme order statistic, usually pinned at the MTU or at a TSO segment size, so its relative change is ~0 punctuated by single-packet spikes.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: Can exceed the link MTU when the capture point sees TSO/LRO-coalesced segments (values up to 64240 are present in the real March-2 captures). That is a property of where the capture was taken, not a parsing error, and is left unclipped.

features.name: payload_zero_ratio
features.aggregation: count(payload_len == 0) / count(IP packets), per window
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 means every packet carried payload
features.relative_change_reason: Bounded proportion whose level is the informative quantity; its relative change is a small bounded number that duplicates the level.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: payload_nonzero_ratio is EXCLUDED as exactly 1 - payload_zero_ratio: an affine duplicate carries no information a linear model or a network cannot already reach.

features.name: payload_len_entropy
features.aggregation: Shannon entropy (base 2) of the empirical distribution of payload LENGTH VALUES
features.formula: -sum(p * log2(p + 1e-12)) over value_counts(payload_len) / total; 0.0 when <= 1 distinct length. Identical formula to the V4 dst_port_entropy / protocol_entropy.
features.missing_value_rule: the window does not exist — a window with no IP packets produces no row at all
features.zero_value_behaviour: EXACTLY 0.0 when every packet in the window has the same payload length — the classic fixed-size beacon signature — and also for a single-packet window
features.relative_change_reason: Consistent with the frozen V4 convention, which gives dst_port_entropy and protocol_entropy relative changes. An entropy collapse (traffic becoming uniformly sized, i.e. beacon-like) is a transition, not a level.
features.parity_note: single shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) used by both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point; verified numerically across two independent invocation routes
features.notes: THIS IS A LENGTH-DISTRIBUTION ENTROPY, NOT BYTE-VALUE SHANNON ENTROPY. No payload byte is ever read by any part of this pipeline; the only input is the integer length from the IP/L4 headers. The two quantities are routinely confused and measure different things: byte-value entropy detects encryption/compression of content, length entropy detects regularity of message sizes.

features.aggregation_window: 10s vs the preceding EXISTING packet-window row
features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 when the feature is unchanged between adjacent windows
features.relative_change_reason: Denominator is a hop count that is never near zero in a non-empty window, so the ratio is numerically stable. A shift in mean hop distance between adjacent windows is exactly the 'new peer population' signal the world model should see as a transition.
features.parity_note: same shared implementation as the base feature
features.notes: identical transform semantics to the 26 frozen V4 relative-change features

features.zero_value_behaviour: 0.0 when the feature is unchanged between adjacent windows

That saturation is retained deliberately: constant-TTL -> varied-TTL is a genuine regime change and the clipped value is a correct 'large jump' indicator, not a numerical accident. Same behaviour the frozen V4 contract already accepts for std_pkt_len.

features.parity_note: same shared implementation as the base feature
